draft.title: Population distribution and density
card: the pattern of where people live across an area. It can be even, or clustered in some places and sparse in others.
the number of people per square kilometre. Population density = total population ÷ land area.
People cluster where life is easier: near fresh water, on fertile land, where jobs are found and where the climate is mild. Few people live in places that are very dry, very cold, steep or remote.
Density is an average over a whole area. A region can have a low density even if most of its people live crowded together in one small part of it.
draft.remember: Distribution is where people live. Density is how many people per square kilometre.

a.q: Which of these best describes population distribution?
opts: The pattern of where people live across an area
The number of people living in each square kilometre
The number of people living in a country's cities
The change in the number of people over time
a.why: Distribution is about the pattern of where people are spread out or clustered. The option about people per square kilometre describes density, which is a measure of crowding and not of pattern.
a.clue: Think about a map showing where the dots of people fall.

b.q: Country X has 2 million people and a land area of 100 000 km². Most of them live in one coastal city. Which statement is correct?
opts: Its density is 20 people per km², but it is clustered
Its density is 20 people per km² and it is evenly spread
Its density is 200 people per km², but it is clustered
Its density is 200 people per km² and it is evenly spread
b.why: Density = 2 000 000 ÷ 100 000 = 20 people per km². Most people live in one city, so the distribution is clustered, even though the average density is low. Density is an average and does not show where people live.
b.clue: Divide the population by the land area, then ask where people actually live.

a.best: The pattern of where people live across an area

b.best: Its density is 20 people per km², but it is clustered
